candidates: In sphinx-gallery example files, keep narrative comments concise — remove trailing remarks that restate what is already obvious from context (e.g., noting that an interactive viewer 'might be preferred' after already explaining it provides an interactive view).

When a sphinx-gallery tutorial example includes hardcoded numeric data (e.g., arrays of atomic positions or cell parameters), add a brief note explaining where those values come from or how they were obtained, rather than presenting unexplained magic numbers to the reader.

Ensure prose descriptions in tutorial/example comments accurately name the actual Python operators and ASE methods used in the adjacent code; do not describe an operation using a different method name (e.g., do not say 'extend' when the code actually uses the `+` operator / `Atoms.__add__`).

Use full, descriptive variable names throughout sphinx-gallery example and tutorial code; avoid single-letter or abbreviated names (e.g., use `water` rather than `W`) because examples serve as learning references and abbreviated names obscure meaning.
